_note: JSON sidecar for migration-manifest.yaml. The wizard runtime CLI consumes JSON; YAML is the human-facing companion. Both files MUST stay in sync.

artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/capability_run: Setting up a capability's safe, read-only view of the outside system now asks which file declares that it provides one, instead of guessing a filename from the capability's id -- so a project whose files were named before that convention existed now works. When it cannot be worked out, the message says which of the three things went wrong and names the file: more than one file claims the same kind of access, a file's declaration cannot be read, or the file could not be loaded. The reader object itself still comes only from the registry that checks it is a real reader, never straight out of the file that declared it.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/topology.py: New file. Reads what each of this project's own external-access files declares it provides -- the operation kind it registers a reader or an adapter for -- and answers "which file serves this?" from those declarations, so a file's name is never part of the answer. It reads the files as text and never runs them, so working this out can never execute any of your project's code as a side effect. A registration it cannot read is reported by name and line number rather than quietly skipped, because a quiet skip is exactly what hid the problem this fixes.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/zones.py: Records the new kernel-side test file alongside the kernel module it tests, in the list of files that are part of the safe write kernel itself rather than capability code. No change to what any capability may do.

migrations.migration_steps: 1. Run the update check (it reports what's new + the recommendation). 2. On the operator's yes, the assistant applies it ("${{WIZARD_HOME:-$HOME/agent-wizard}}/scripts/wizard" self-upgrade --to v0.22.0 --apply). 3. A backup is taken first; the operator's own data, rules, credentials, and logs are never touched.
migrations.notes: Minor-additive release to v0.22.0. A capability's safe, read-only access to the outside system is now found by what a file declares it provides, rather than by what the file is named. Before this, that lookup expected an exact naming pattern, so a project whose files were set up before that pattern existed could fail here even though everything it needed was already in place; it now works correctly for that kind of project too. If a capability's read-only file exists but what it declares cannot be read -- for example, a registration written inside a function instead of at the top level of the file -- the message you get now names that exact file, instead of the generic message telling you the capability itself needs to be rebuilt. The notices an upgrade produces are more accurate and more specific too. A test file is now told apart from a file your system actually runs: it is told plainly that nothing running uses it and there is nothing for you to do, rather than being told, wrongly, that its outside access was switched off and it needs rebuilding. That notice, and the summary printed when an upgrade finishes, now show each flagged file's full location rather than just its name, so two files that happen to share a name in different folders are no longer shown as if they were the same file. When an upgrade cannot read what a file has registered, it now says so plainly and names that file, instead of quietly pointing at a different, unrelated file as the cause, and writes that into your pending-work list as its own item. And after you record a decision to leave a flagged file exactly as it is, the notice now says plainly that this did not switch anything back on -- it only means that file stops holding up the rest of your system. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
migrations.preflight: Verify the operator project carries a .wizard/manifest.json whose foundation_bundle_version is v0.21.0 (or any version in the supported range). A backup is taken automatically.
migrations.rollback: Restore from .wizard/backups/pre-v0.22.0/ and set foundation_bundle_version back to v0.21.0.

migrations.notes: Minor-additive release to v0.22.0. A capability's safe, read-only access to the outside system is now found by what a file declares it provides, rather than by what the file is named. Before this, that lookup expected an exact naming pattern, so a project whose files were set up before that pattern existed could fail here even though everything it needed was already in place; it now works correctly for that kind of project too. If a capability's read-only file exists but what it declares cannot be read -- for example, a registration written inside a function instead of at the top level of the file -- the message you get now names that exact file, instead of the generic message telling you the capability itself needs to be rebuilt. The notices an upgrade produces are more accurate and more specific too. A test file is now told apart from a file your system actually runs: it is told plainly that nothing running uses it and there is nothing for you to do, rather than being told, wrongly, that its outside access was switched off and it needs rebuilding. That notice, and the summary printed when an upgrade finishes, now show each flagged file's full location rather than just its name, so two files that happen to share a name in different folders are no longer shown as if they were the same file. When an upgrade cannot read what a file has registered, it now says so plainly and names that file, instead of quietly pointing at a different, unrelated file as the cause, and writes that into your pending-work list as its own item. And after you record a decision to leave a flagged file exactly as it is, the notice now says plainly that this did not switch anything back on -- it only means that file stops holding up the rest of your system. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
